newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo cbank surprises marts with unch discount rate.
newsitem.headline: Yugo cbank surprises marts with unch discount rate.

text.p: The National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) left its key discount rate unchanged in February at 4.5 percent per month, or an annual 77.5 percent, a central bank official told Reuters on Monday.
February's unchanged discount rate, the ninth consecutive steady rate, surprised traders who had expected a rise this month.

Though the NBY said last week it had no plans to change its discount rate policy in 1997, some traders had interpreted the central bank's launch of its new tranche of 30-day bonds at an annual 147.48 percent two weeks ago as signs that the weighted interest rates and the discount rate would rise.
"We thought higher rates on NBY's bonds were a prelude to a tighter monetary policy. But right now, I really have no comment," one trader said.

But a central bank official who asked not to be named said "the (unchanged discount) rate is in line with current and expected monetary developments, price movements and an average rate on central bank short-term bonds sold via the Belgrade bourse."

NBY sets its discount rate each month using a basket that includes interest rates on the open money market, short-term bonds, price rises, expected monetary developments, credit demand and money supply.
The discount rate is said to be the NBY's key instrument in regulating market liquidity.
It was first cut to 4.5 percent in June from 6.31 percent in May 1996.
The discount rate will remain positive in real terms and depend on retail price increases and interest rates on the local financial market, NBY Vice-Governor Ratko Banovic said.

Another trader said the discount rate was probably kept unchanged because the NBY had extended too many credits and that a higher discount rate would put additional strain on otherwise insolvent borrowers.
"NBY had to do this. It gave commercial banks some breathing space instead of increasing their borrowing costs," a central bank source said.
